name: Inversions After Shuffle
description: You are given a permutation of integers from 1 to n . Exactly once you apply the following operation to this permutation: pick a random segment and shuffle its elements. Formally: Pick a random segment (continuous subsequence) from l to r . All segments are equiprobable. Let k = r - l + 1 , i.e. the length of the chosen segment. Pick a random permutation of integers from 1 to k , p 1 , p 2 , ..., p k . All k ! permutation are equiprobable. This permutation is applied to elements of the chosen segment, i.e. permutation a 1 , a 2 , ..., a l - 1 , a l , a l + 1 , ..., a r - 1 , a r , a r + 1 , ..., a n is transformed to a 1 , a 2 , ..., a l - 1 , a l - 1 + p 1 , a l - 1 + p 2 , ..., a l - 1 + p k - 1 , a l - 1 + p k , a r + 1 , ..., a n . Inversion if a pair of elements (not necessary neighbouring) with the wrong relative order. In other words, the number of inversion is equal to the number of pairs ( i , j ) such that i < j and a i > a j . Find the expected number of inversions after we apply exactly one operation mentioned above.
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer n ( 1 ≤ n ≤ 100 000 ) — the length of the permutation. The second line contains n distinct integers from 1 to n — elements of the permutation.
output_specification: Print one real value — the expected number of inversions. Your answer will be considered correct if its absolute or relative error does not exceed 10 - 9 .
